label: Real run on this Mac's kind cluster (Kubernetes in Docker, from our own manifests in deploy/kind), with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 5 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; the request was denied (not the request's id, typed at a terminal), and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

fault.name: duplicate-delivery
fault.title: Payments counted twice in the books
fault.cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer without its dedupe (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive): every webhook the provider sends again, after an acknowledgement it never got, is booked a second time
expected_symptoms: the money check fails: events counted twice, the books ahead of the provider by their amounts
the webhook dashboard stays green, and consumer lag stays at 0
the ledger stops reporting 'already processed' while the confirmer still sees the same duplicates
fault.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to the idempotent handler, then repair each double posting with a reversal (a write, so it needs approval)

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 21:39:39Z (revision 2) with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. That handler books every Kafka message it reads without checking whether the event_id is already in the ledger. Webhooks are resent until acknowledged and Kafka delivers at least once, so one provider event can appear on provider-events more than once (evt_000308 sat at offsets 100, 101 and 103). Each copy was posted as its own balanced transaction. So ledger_balanced passes, but provider_clearing is inflated: posted_exactly_once fails for 7 events and matches_provider is off by +$461.00. Payments and refunds still match the provider, so only the ledger is wrong. Still open: whether every duplicate came after 21:39:39 (the alert fired 17 s after the deploy, but earlier postings were not checked), and whether the duplicates came from provider retries or from the receiver.

evidence.shows: Confirms the alert. 7 events were posted 2 or 3 times (evt_000308 three times), and the ledger is +$461.00 against the provider. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds agree with the provider, so the error is confined to the ledger's double bookings.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 21:39:39Z (revision 2) with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, 17 s before the alert fired. No other service changed since the initial rollout at 21:37:29.

ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000308 ($131.93) three times, from offsets provider-events/0＠100, ＠101 and ＠103 (21:39:53–55). Each redelivered copy was booked again, with no dedup by event_id.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its previous revision, so that its earlier handler returns and new duplicate postings stop. Then do a separate data repair: reverse the extra ledger transactions the money check names (for example 255, 266, 272, 273, 297, plus the extras for evt_000298 and evt_000308), keeping one posting per event. Re-run money_check to confirm that all invariants pass.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated. Events queue in Kafka under its consumer group and are processed when it returns, so ledger postings are delayed briefly but nothing is lost. Payments, refunds, payment-confirmer and webhook-receiver are not affected. The rollback does not remove the bad postings already made; those need the manual repair. Reversing the wrong transaction ids in that repair could create new mismatches.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rolled-back revision misbehaves, redeploy ledger-consumer with revision 2's settings or the last known-good settings. Watch klaxon_consumer_events_total, the Kafka consumer lag and money_check. For the data repair, record every reversing entry so that it can itself be reversed.
